papers.title: Receiver-Resolution APS-PDP Maps for Wireless Channels: Benchmarking and Coarse-to-Fine Modeling
papers.abstract: Angle Power Spectrum (APS) and Power Delay Profile (PDP) are receiver-facing spectra that govern beam selection and wideband equalization. Most ray-tracing benchmarks provide supervision as variable-size multipath component lists. This format does not match practical receivers, whose angular and delay resolutions are limited by array aperture and system bandwidth. As a result, learning targets are ambiguous and evaluations can change with reconstruction conventions. We introduce UrbanADPSMap, a benchmark that converts ray-traced supervision into fixed-grid APS and PDP targets by explicitly modeling bandwidth-limited and aperture-limited response kernels. By fixing the receiver-domain kernels, discretization, and validity mask, UrbanADPSMap removes reconstruction-induced target ambiguity and stabilizes downstream evaluation across methods. Built on this benchmark, we propose SpecFlowAR, a coarse-to-fine generator based on multi-scale autoregressive flow matching. The model first captures coarse dispersion structure and then refines beam-relevant peaks and low-power tails. The number of function evaluations controls the sampling budget, enabling latency and quality to be adjusted for dense spectrum queries. Experiments on the test set show that SpecFlowAR reduces BPL@5 to 2.03 dB under a unified NFE=80 budget, while improving beam utility and reducing errors of 3GPP dispersion statistics.

papers.title: PENSA: A Spatial Accelerator for BitNet b1.58 Inference on an HBM-equipped AMD Alveo FPGA
papers.abstract: Ternary large language models (tLLMs) replace general multiplication in dominant linear layers with sign-controlled accumulation, shifting hardware bottlenecks toward packed-weight delivery, reduction, and operator occupancy. PENSA is an end-to-end FPGA accelerator for the BitNet b1.58 2B4T model on an AMD Alveo U50. Two row-partitioned ternary matrix engines consume packed TQ1_0 weights from eight independent high-bandwidth memory (HBM) pseudo-channels, each processing 1,280 ternary weights per cycle through sign selection and integer reduction. The sequencer, attention, and vocabulary-projection units remain resident on the FPGA, while two-stream interleaved scheduling overlaps sequences across the persistent pipeline to form the Penta-Unit. At 104.1~MHz, PENSA achieves 58.09 tok/s at context 128 and 24.60 tok/s at context 2048, corresponding to 2.14-3.14$\times$ the throughput of a same-model Xeon E-2356G baseline. The resulting system demonstrates end-to-end FPGA execution of 2B-scale BitNet topology without modifying its model structure.

papers.title: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: We present UltraVoxelGS, a 3D ultrasound reconstruction method that achieves both fast reconstruction and physically faithful rendering for the first time, bringing live spatial feedback during 2D ultrasound scanning within reach. This is made possible by a feed-forward design that predicts a complete Gaussian scene representation from posed ultrasound images directly, entirely bypassing the per-scene optimization bottleneck that has confined prior methods to offline use. Realising such feed-forward prediction in this setting is non-trivial: unlike natural images, ultrasound slices share at most one-dimensional intersections and exhibit view-dependent appearance due to acoustic propagation and attenuation, violating the dense overlap and photometric consistency assumed by existing feed-forward Gaussian methods. Hence, to achieve fast reconstruction, we introduce a feed-forward voxel-to-Gaussian pass that decouples representation size from input count by lifting all posed slices into a fixed-size voxel support and predicting Gaussian parameters directly. For faithful rendering, we propose ultrasound-aware appearance rendering strategy factorize reflection from cumulative attenuation during training and exploit appearance continuity among spatially adjacent slices for efficient Render-time Appearance Adaptation. On both real-world and simulated datasets, UltraVoxelGS achieves best PSNR/SSIM compared with per-scene optimization baselines while reducing inference from 10-20 minutes to approximately 10 seconds (over 35 times faster) and scales to sequences exceeding 1,000 frames. Code is available at https://github.com/YuebyYue/UltraVoxelGS-camera-ready.

papers.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
papers.abstract: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. Unlike recent TTS pipelines, WaveGen does not rely on separately trained or externally decoded intermediate representations, such as neural audio codecs, Mel-spectrogram vocoders, or VAE-based latent models. In addition, WaveGen performs internal text-speech alignment within a single model, eliminating the need for external alignment modules such as duration predictors. To preserve a truly end-to-end formulation, our framework further avoids dependence on self-supervised representations, such as BERT-based text embeddings and Wav2Vec 2.0-based semantic representations, as well as semantic distillation methods for training optimization. To achieve this, we carefully design Spectral Forcing, a model architecture with disentangled diffusion heads, and a training objective based on a multi-scale spectral $v$-loss. We further validate the scalability of end-to-end TTS models by scaling the model size from 0.1B to 0.6B parameters. Using a single architecture, open-source data, and one-stage training, without external modules such as duration predictor or REPA, WaveGen demonstrates fully end-to-end waveform generation achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Emilia training dataset. In particular, WaveGen achieves a WER of 1.47 and a SIM of 0.75 on the Seed-en benchmark. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/sh-lee-prml/WaveGen

papers.title: Mechanistic Interpretability with Sparse Autoencoder Neural Operators
papers.abstract: We introduce sparse autoencoder neural operators (SAE-NOs), a new class of sparse autoencoders that operate in function spaces rather than fixed-dimensional Euclidean representations. We formalize the functional representation hypothesis, where data are explained through sparse compositions of structured functions. Unlike standard SAEs that represent concepts with scalar activations, SAE-NOs parameterize concepts as functions, enabling representations that capture not only a concept's presence, but also how and where it is expressed across the input domain. We achieve this through joint sparsity: concept sparsity selects active concepts, while domain sparsity governs where they are expressed. We instantiate this framework using Fourier neural operators (SAE-FNOs), parameterizing concepts as integral operators in the Fourier domain. This functional and spectral parameterization is particularly advantageous when data exhibit spatial structure across scales or when concepts are frequency-structured. We characterize SAE-FNO on vision data and demonstrate that it learns localized patterns, uses concepts more efficiently, and exhibits stable concept characteristics across sparsity levels. We further show that SAE-FNO adapts to changes in domain size and generalizes across discretizations, operating at resolutions beyond those seen during training, where standard SAEs fail. We also introduce lifting into SAEs and show theoretically and empirically that it acts as a preconditioner that accelerates optimization. Overall, our results show that moving from vector-valued to functional parameterizations, with concept and domain sparsity, extends SAEs from representing concept presence to modeling structured concept expression, highlighting the importance of parameterization.

papers.title: Neural Signals Generate Clinical Notes in the Wild
papers.abstract: Generating clinical reports that summarize abnormal patterns, diagnostic findings, and clinical interpretations from long-term EEG recordings remains labor-intensive. We present CELM, the first clinical EEG-to-Language foundation model capable of summarizing long-duration, variable-length EEG recordings and performing end-to-end clinical report generation at multiple scales. CELM integrates pretrained EEG foundation models with language models to enable scalable multimodal learning. We curate a large-scale clinical EEG dataset containing 9,922 reports paired with approximately 11,000 hours of EEG recordings from 9,048 patients to train CELM, and release the benchmark pipeline, with automated report-structuring, to facilitate future research. Experimental results show that CELM consistently outperforms existing methods across all evaluation settings. Importantly, we further conduct human evaluation with clinical experts, demonstrating that CELM generates reports that are more clinically coherent, diagnostically reliable, and better aligned with expert interpretation. We release our model code and benchmark construction pipeline at https://github.com/Jathurshan0330/CELM.

papers.title: PPG2ECG: Physiology-Guided Latent Rectified Flow for Electro-Hemodynamic PPG-to-ECG Generation
papers.abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical standard for cardiac assessment but requires dedicated hardware that does not scale to daily-life monitoring. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearables but lacks ECG-specific diagnostic morphology and is corrupted by motion and sensor noise. PPG-to-ECG generation aims to bridge this gap by recovering electrical morphology and timing from peripheral pulse signals. However, existing methods largely rely on statistical alignment and data-driven generation. They fail to explicitly structure the latent space around physiology-aware electro-hemodynamic factors and lack constraints from forward physiological dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose PPG2ECG, a physiology-guided latent rectified flow framework. PPG2ECG introduces an electro-hemodynamic simulator that co-models ECG and PPG through shared cardiac phase dynamics. Guided by this simulator, a Physiology-Aware AutoEncoder learns a structured electro-hemodynamic latent space. Then we integrate this simulator guidance into a PPG-conditioned latent rectified flow, enforcing ECG-side morphology consistency and ECG-to-PPG forward hemodynamic consistency during generative transport. Experiments on the large-scale MC-MED dataset demonstrate that PPG2ECG significantly improves PPG-to-ECG generation and downstream cardiovascular disease classification, proving its ability to generate ECGs that are both signal-faithful and physiologically plausible under the ECG-to-PPG hemodynamic pathway

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
papers.abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

papers.title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
papers.abstract: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.

papers.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.

papers.title: Joint LSFC and Nakagami-m Estimation From Downlink SINR in GZF-Precoded CF-mMIMO
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) is important for reliability-sensitive cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems. This paper proposes a joint estimation method for link-specific large-scale fading coefficients (LSFCs) and a common Nakagami-$m$ shape parameter using power and downlink SINR measurements. A tractable SINR distribution is first derived under global zero-forcing (GZF) precoding, Nakagami-$m$ fading, and link-level fractional power control (FPC). Based on the derived probability density function (PDF), a model-driven neural network (NN) is developed to solve the resulting maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) problem. Simulations show that the reconstructed SINR distributions obtained with the estimated parameters closely match the empirical distributions. With $2 \times 10^{5}$ samples, the proposed method achieves an LSFC root-mean-square error (RMSE) of approximately 1.0 dB and an $m$ RMSE of approximately 0.085.

papers.title: MambaPD: Bidirectional Selective State Space Model for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Resting-State EEG
papers.abstract: Typical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) occurs only after significant dopaminergic loss, while resting-state EEG abnormalities like alpha slowing and reduced coherence occur earlier. While many published EEG-based PD detectors claim accuracy greater than 95%, many use epoch-level splits which leak subject identity. I introduce MambaPD, a bidirectional selective state space model for resting-state EEG-based PD detection, blending the channel mixing, patch tokenization and bidirectional Mamba encoder. It is compared with four baselines (TCN, BiLSTM with attention, EEGNet and a patch Transformer) in two public datasets (UNM, SanDiego) using subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation (checkpoints were selected on the held-out fold, so absolute estimates are optimistic). On UNM the accuracy is between 0.67 and 0.71, and MambaPD (0.714) is not statistically distinguishable from the Transformer (0.715), and TCN (0.708), with the highest sensitivity (0.82), while the lowest specificity (0.52). For the smaller SanDiego cohort, accuracy is in the range of 0.60 to 0.70, with the highest scores (0.703) from TCN and the lowest (0.601) from EEGNet, while MambaPD scores 0.631, with the lowest specificity (0.46) among the five models. The differences among the models on UNM are minor compared to the differences among folds. I report the whole pipeline, per-fold results, and the shortcomings of the protocol.

papers.title: Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits
papers.abstract: Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.

papers.title: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems
papers.abstract: Traditional communication resource allocation optimizes operational metrics such as rate, latency, energy efficiency, and reliability. Motivated by goal-oriented semantic communication, we develop a generalized allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them via expected utility, cumulative prospect theory (CPT), or related decision criteria. The formulation separates operational rewards, user-side valuations, and system-level decision criteria under uncertainty. We characterize utilities incorporating QoS/service reference levels, deficit sensitivity, post-reference saturation, and loss aversion. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, $\alpha$-fairness, and stochastic expected utility maximization emerge as exact special cases, while soft QoS-aware allocation follows from a deficit-penalty generalization. For deterministic orthogonal systems, we derive utility-weighted marginal-reward KKT conditions characterizing global optimality under concave composite objectives. For nonorthogonal and stochastic systems, we develop successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithms and establish stationary-point guarantees under explicit smooth and composite nonsmooth assumptions, including a CPT branch-stationarity result under eventual nondegenerate ordering identification. For globally solved penalized problems, we derive an $O(1/\lambda)$ bound on excess aggregate soft-QoS deficit, and on the deficit itself whenever a QoS-feasible allocation exists. Additionally, we establish an $O(1/\epsilon^2)$ outer iteration bound for the smooth fixed-step SCA best-response residual. Numerical examples demonstrate how reference points, marginal utility slopes, channel quality, and resource budgets influence active users and allocation policies.

papers.title: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements
papers.abstract: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites serve unmodified LTE phones today from low Earth orbit, where the satellite's motion creates Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. Since large offsets such as these cannot be compensated adequately by the user equipment (UE), the satellite pre-compensates the Doppler shift of each beam, but it can do so for only one reference point in the beam. A UE elsewhere in the beam still has to compensate a residual offset; previous field studies report residuals of up to 10 kHz, beyond the $\pm$7.5 kHz that the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing can resolve. In this paper we corroborate this effect with our own detailed measurements of Starlink transmissions and further correlate ineffective handover performance to inadequate residual offset compensation. We analyze the Doppler compensation problem with detailed standard-specific simulations and propose a compensation method at the UE, based on the location of the UE with respect to the beam reference point used for the Doppler compensation and the known satellite location, that improves the efficiency of handover. With UE cell-specific pre-compensation, the neighbors are identified, read correctly and handed over to in time rather than lost to radio-link failure.

papers.title: Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.abstract: The Karhunen-Lo\`eve transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.

papers.title: Deep learning for structural health monitoring: An application to heritage structures
papers.abstract: Thanks to recent advancements in numerical methods, computer power, and monitoring technology, seismic ambient noise provides precious information about the structural behavior of old buildings. The measurement of the vibrations produced by anthropic and environmental sources and their use for dynamic identification and structural health monitoring of buildings initiated an emerging, cross-disciplinary field engaging seismologists, engineers, mathematicians, and computer scientists. In this work, we employ recent deep learning techniques for time-series forecasting to inspect and detect anomalies in the large dataset recorded during a long-term monitoring campaign conducted on the San Frediano bell tower in Lucca. We frame the problem as an unsupervised anomaly detection task and train a Temporal Fusion Transformer to learn the normal dynamics of the structure. We then detect the anomalies by looking at the differences between the predicted and observed frequencies.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.

papers.title: Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Nonlinear Matrix Decompositions
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for solving nonlinear matrix decompositions (NMD). Given an input matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and a factorization rank $r \ll \min(m, n)$, NMD seeks matrices $W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times r}$ and $H \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n}$ such that $X \approx f(WH)$, where $f$ is an element-wise nonlinear function. We evaluate our method on several representative nonlinear models: the rectified linear unit activation $f(x) = \max(0, x)$, suitable for nonnegative sparse data approximation, the component-wise square $f(x) = x^2$, applicable to probabilistic circuit representation, and the MinMax transform $f(x) = \min(b, \max(a, x))$, relevant for recommender systems. The proposed framework flexibly supports diverse loss functions, including least squares, $\ell_1$ norm, and the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and can be readily extended to other nonlinearities and metrics. We illustrate the applicability, efficiency, and adaptability of the approach on real-world datasets, highlighting its potential for a broad range of applications.

papers.title: The Resurrection of Spectrum Spreading for 6G and Beyond: From Sinusoids to Chirps
papers.abstract: Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) and its sinusoidal subcarriers have underpinned the 4G and 5G eras, delivering high spectral efficiency and resilience to multipath fading through an efficient multicarrier architecture. However, as future systems move toward doubly dispersive environments driven by high-mobility applications and migration to mmWave/sub-THz bands, the time-invariance assumption underlying OFDM becomes increasingly difficult to maintain, and Doppler-induced degradation becomes prominent. While enhancements such as MIMO, advanced coding, and scheduling provide incremental remedies, they introduce additional overhead, because the sinusoidal subcarrier itself offers no inherent waveform-level robustness to Doppler impairments. Accordingly, two time-frequency spreading philosophies have emerged to improve Doppler resilience by distributing each symbol's energy across both dimensions of the time-frequency plane: (i) 2D isotropic spreading via the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, exemplified by the orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) family, and (ii) sheared spreading via parameterizable chirps, exemplified by the affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM) family. In this article, we examine key considerations for future waveform design across these paradigms and argue that transitioning from the sinusoidal subcarriers of OFDM to the chirp-based subcarriers offers a viable design direction for improving Doppler robustness while retaining much of the mature OFDM infrastructure. This perspective also highlights the suitability of chirp-based waveforms for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) and their extensibility to emerging physical-layer techniques. Overall, we argue that the transition from sinusoids to chirps is a technically motivated, compelling evolutionary direction for future wireless physical layer design.

papers.title: L-FAME: Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation EEG Dataset and Benchmark
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation Electroencephalography (L-FAME) dataset and an accompanying benchmark, designed to foster research into the neural effects of various meditation practices and the evolution of these effects over a six-week training period. The dataset includes baseline EEG recordings from 74 healthy college participants, of whom 44 completed the six-week intervention and returned for post-intervention recordings, along with psychological assessments. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three distinct meditation groups: two mantra-based techniques (SA-TA-NA-MA and Hare Krishna) and one Breath Focus practice. Leveraging this unique longitudinal and comparative dataset, we propose a benchmark suite comprising three distinct classification tasks: (1) cognitive state decoding to distinguish between resting and meditation states, (2) fine-grained classification of the specific meditation techniques, and (3) cross-session adaptation to evaluate model generalization across the longitudinal time gap. We provide comprehensive baseline results for these tasks utilizing a range of classical machine learning algorithms and deep learning architectures. The complete dataset, preprocessing pipelines, and benchmark evaluation code are being publicly released, offering a valuable resource and a standardized framework for the development and comparison of new analytical methods in computational meditation research and EEG-based machine learning. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/L-FAME-Dataset-Benchmark/L-FAME

papers.title: A Scale-Space Theory of Memory
papers.abstract: Scale-space theory has emerged as a central attempt to restrict the {\it general} theory of signal processing with geometric constraints inspired from the animal world. In the mathematical language of operator theory, scale-space theory restricts the Toeplitz operator. The present paper investigates scale-space theory for memory systems. We investigate how scale space theory restricts a memory system encoding past information, that is, restricts the Hankel operator. Our main result is to establish a close correspondence between scale-space theory and the long-studied {\it relaxation} property.

papers.title: From Discrete Snapshots to Geometric Entity: Motion-Native Channel Tracking for THz Near-Field XL-MIMO
papers.abstract: Channel tracking in mobile terahertz (THz) near-field extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems is challenging because spherical-wave propagation couples angle and range, leading to rapid and nonlinear channel evolution under sparse pilot observations. Existing approaches typically estimate pilot-local channel or position snapshots before applying temporal tracking or smoothing, making them vulnerable to information loss during snapshot formation. To break this bottleneck, we propose a paradigm shift from tracking discrete snapshots to estimating a holistic geometric entity, namely, one shared continuous UE trajectory over the tracking window. Specifically, we parameterize the trajectory using a low-dimensional cubic B-spline representation and directly couple the per-pilot profile likelihoods through this shared trajectory before any pilot-local position estimate is finalized, thereby inducing continuous near-field channel evolution. We further characterize the efficient geometric information supplied by each pilot observation and its aggregation in the shared spline-coefficient space. Based on this formulation, we develop a regularized maximum a posteriori estimator and a quadratic-penalty lifted solver that separates parallel pilot-local geometric updates from a structured global spline update. The resulting global system is banded and, for a fixed spline degree, admits linear-complexity factorization, enabling an efficient structured implementation. Simulations demonstrate consistently improved tracking accuracy over representative temporally refined baselines in the tested medium-to-high-SNR regime, together with a favorable accuracy--runtime trade-off. These results highlight the benefit of coupling sparse pilot observations through a shared continuous trajectory rather than temporally processing independently estimated snapshots.

papers.title: Modified CNN-Learned Surrogate Covariance With Krylov/Lanczos Subspace for DoA Estimation
papers.abstract: Recently, learning-based approaches have been employed to improve the robustness of subspace methods in DoA estimation. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was used as a data-driven framework employing an autoencoder to generate a well-conditioned surrogate covariance optimized end-to-end through a differentiable classical estimator, such as the Root-MUSIC. The complete system is designed to estimate the directions of arrival based on a spectral decomposition using the EVD of this covariance matrix. In this work, a new approach is proposed by formulating the spectral stage of the Root-MUSIC algorithm in terms of the orthogonal complement of the signal subspace, thereby eliminating the need for the noise subspace and noise eigenvalues. Furthermore, the full EVD is replaced by a Lanczos tridiagonalization with reorthogonalization, reducing the overall computational cost.

papers.title: Missed Interferers in Ray-Traced Radio Maps: A Digital-Twin and Stochastic Geometry Study of Aerial Coverage
papers.abstract: Ray-traced digital twins are increasingly used to plan where cellular-connected uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) can fly. In this paper, we build a Sionna RT digital twin around Raleigh, NC, with 18,591 buildings and two overlapping sub-1 GHz operator networks, and study the downlink signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of UAVs at 40-300 m. We show that the Monte Carlo radio-map solver of Sionna RT misses distant line-of-sight (LOS) interferers on aerial planes. With $10^7$ rays per sector and 5 m cells, it therefore underestimates the coverage at low SINR thresholds and overestimates it at high thresholds, by up to 26 percentage points at $\pm$2 dB and 50-100 m. Using a LOS-aware deterministic engine validated with Sionna's path solver, we then develop a stochastic geometry model with strongest-sector association and own-site leakage that matches the engine without fitting. The analysis shows that the interference grows logarithmically with the modeled network radius, so a twin that omits distant LOS sites overestimates the coverage, and that altitude mainly reduces the coverage at high SINR thresholds. Finally, selecting the better of two operators raises the minimum SINR along the best corridor by 1.0-3.9 dB up to 100 m.

papers.title: Real-Time Trans-Oceanic Fiber Sensing via Convergence of Long-Reach OFDR, High-Speed Optical Networking, and RDMA-Capable Edge-GPUs
papers.abstract: We demonstrate real-time network-integrated bi-directional fiber sensing over a 4400-km subsea cable. Streaming and fusing two OFDR instruments via RDMA over a live transoceanic 130Gbaud coherent link and GPU edge-compute enabling parallel capture of multiple spatial resolutions from ~10m to ~100m.

papers.title: Two-Timescale Receive Combining for Fronthaul-Constrained Uplink XL-MIMO with Visibility Regions
papers.abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) arrays are hard to deploy in virtualized radio access networks, because the fronthaul data rate grows with the number of antennas when the radio unit forwards every antenna sample. We propose a two-timescale receiver that allocates the per-user combining ranks under the fronthaul stream budget from the channel statistics. The radio unit applies the long-timescale transform, after which the distributed unit applies a minimum mean-squared-error receiver in the reduced dimension. For disjoint visibility regions, we prove that the reduced-dimension receiver decouples across users. We characterize the sum-rate loss to second order and show that the greedy allocation, which we call saturating capture, minimizes its leading term. In simulations, the allocation gains over a uniform-rank baseline, matches a budget-trimmed threshold rule at a small number of users and exceeds it as the array and the user count grow. The gain grows with the heterogeneity of the per-user eigenvalue profiles and vanishes for identical profiles. Under out-of-cell interference offset by at least half a window width, the gain survives with clean covariances, which window-restricted estimation keeps for disjoint windows.

papers.title: Coexistence of LEO Satellite Communication Systems under Regulatory Protection Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the coexistence of two low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems sharing the same frequency band: a primary system with regulatory precedence over the spectrum and a secondary system that must not cause excessive interference to the primary system's ground users. This spectrum sharing paradigm was recently formalized by the United States Federal Communications Commission (FCC) through short-term and long-term protection criteria that limit primary-link unavailability and throughput degradation due to interference inflicted by the secondary system. To facilitate coexistence, we propose a satellite selection mechanism that associates the secondary system's satellites with clusters of ground cells at each handover to maximize secondary-user throughput while abiding by these regulatory constraints. Our mechanism enforces both constraints through a cumulative assessment that combines past primary-link performance with predicted performance over the upcoming handover interval. Simulation results show that our proposed method achieves up to 31% higher secondary-user throughput than prior work that imposes interference-to-noise ratio (INR) constraints, even when its constraints are tuned to satisfy the FCC's throughput-based protection criteria.

papers.title: Soft-then-Hard: Joint Link Association and Precoding Optimization for LEO Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Spatial multiplexing in dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks is hindered by two bottlenecks. First, line-of-sight (LoS)-dominant propagation from a high orbital altitude places the users in a narrow angular region, which limits the spatial resolution achievable by a single satellite. Second, the visible satellites cause severe inter-satellite interference. Both effects call for joint link association and precoding, because the association decides which users are served together and which streams interfere. However, conventional block coordinate descent with hard association updates suffers from premature turning-off, where an inactive link loses precoder power and cannot be reactivated in subsequent iterations. To overcome this limitation, we propose a soft-then-hard update scheme that relaxes the association into continuous weights via iterative scaling, keeping candidate links active. Annealing progressively concentrates the association weights as the precoders are updated, after which a single hard matching determines the serving links. We further extend this framework to the LEO space-time channel, where distinct Doppler shifts provide user separability beyond angular geometry. Numerical results show that, over the space-time channel, the proposed design outperforms the baselines while effectively exploiting this separability.

papers.title: An Overview on Multimodal Wireless and Visual Sensing for Environment Reconstruction: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.abstract: Physical-scene reconstruction through visual sensing and channel knowledge map (CKM) reconstruction through wireless sensing have attracted growing research interest but have largely evolved independently within the computer vision and wireless communications communities, respectively. When applied to the same physical environment, the two sensing modalities provide complementary observations. Visual sensing captures detailed scene geometry and appearance but is constrained by occlusion and poor lighting. Wireless sensing can provide information beyond visual line of sight regardless of lighting conditions, but its measurements are often sparse and difficult to associate with scene structures. These complementary strengths motivate a unified multimodal approach to physical-scene and CKM reconstruction. This paper provides an overview of such unified environment reconstruction through wireless and visual sensing. We first compare the capabilities and limitations of the two modalities and discuss potential applications that benefit from jointly reconstructing both targets. We then review two complementary research directions, namely wireless-assisted physical-scene reconstruction and vision-assisted CKM reconstruction, highlighting how each modality supports the reconstruction task associated with the other. Building on these perspectives, we discuss design principles for a joint representation that supports both targets and identify mutual refinement, in which each modality helps improve the reconstruction associated with the other. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions, offering insights into developing site-specific environment models for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond networks.
